title: 1Password data breach included some customer info, internal source code
summary: 1Password is reassuring customers that their password vaults are safe after the theft of both account records for a subset of its users and source code from its private repositories. The company said it began investigating the incident on November 19, after it detected indications that an employee’s corporate GitHub account had been breached. The attacker used the account to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, which downloaded what 1Password described as “administrative data” about a subset of users. This included customer names and email addresses, account and user IDs, account creation and last sign-in times, public keys, Secure Remote Password protocol parameters, and “other non-secret account metadata relative to our internal architecture.” Tokens used in some emailed links to customers inviting them to accept provisioning invitations or account recovery were also stolen, although 1Password said that these tokens must be combined with an SSO sign-in or a six-digit confirmation code sent to the user’s registered email address before account access is granted. The company has notified affected customers and, to further secure authentication, has changed the confirmation code format from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric characters. The attacker also copied source code from private repositories and accessed the continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) system; while 1Password said that the source code contained no user secrets, infrastructure secrets in the CI/CD system may have been exposed. The company has triggered a rotation of all relevant credentials. Vaults not affected However, it emphasized, customers’ password vaults were not affected, nor were the keys that protect them. The company also pointed out that it does not store account passwords or secret keys; customers are the only ones who have keys to their vaults. Account recovery keys and 1Password apps and browser extensions are also safe, it said. Actions taken
